newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire recalls Paris envoy after car accident.
newsitem.headline: Zaire recalls Paris envoy after car accident.

text.p: Zaire recalled its ambassador in France on Sunday after he was involved in a car accident in which two French youths were killed last week, a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

Demands that Ambassador Ramazani Baya be brought to trial or ordered out of the country had been mounting after the car he was driving hit the two boys on a pedestrian crossing in the Riviera resort of Menton last Wednesday.
One of the boys, Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killed instantly. The other, 12-year-old Ronald Lehartel, died on Saturday. He had been in a coma in hospital since the accident.
"Following moves by France, the Zairean authorities have let us know they were immediately recalling their ambassador in Paris," the spokesman said.
Baya had travelled to Menton to visit Mobutu, convalescing in nearby Roquebrune Cap Martin from cancer surgery in August.
Police have said Baya, who was driving a hired car, was speeding. A breathalyser test was negative, showing he was under the permitted drinking limit.
Lenoir's parents had demanded that the envoy's diplomatic envoy be waived so that he could be brought to trial for the accident.

The mayor of Menton, Jean-Claude Guibal, and local Gaullist parliamentarian Xavier Beck joined them at the weekend in demanding that the government expel Baya if Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko refused to lift his diplomatic immunity.
The ministry spokesman said that as long as the envoy was in France, he was covered by diplomatic immunity and could not be brought to trial.
"This recall is the diplomatic sanction usual in such cases and does not preclude further moves," he said, apparently indicating that France could try to bring him to court later.
Lehartel died just after some 4,000 people marched through Menton on Saturday in a silent but angry tribute to his friend.
Guibal led the mourners who carried white carnations and lay a wreatch at the seafront pedestrian crossing where the accident occurred.
"We are very angry. (The envoy) is a man like any other and he deserves to be put on trial," said Guillaume, a friend of the two boys.
